mainTopic: Which buildings become impure through נגעים (synagogues, ירושלים), and how a replacement כהן גדול is installed on יום כיפור
overview: This amud continues a contradiction between two ברייתות about whether a בית כנסת can become impure with נגעי בתים. The גמרא first suggests that a big-city synagogue is public property and exempt, while a village synagogue belongs to the locals and can become impure. A challenge from רבי יהודה's view on ירושלים is answered by re-reading his words as 'מקום מקודש', meaning any holy place. The גמרא then explains that the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about whether ירושלים was divided among the שבטים. It brings a ברייתא on how the מקדש was split between יהודה and בנימין, and another ברייתא saying houses in ירושלים may not be rented out because they belong to everyone. From that second ברייתא, אביי learns that a guest should leave his jug and hide for his host. The גמרא then shows that a village synagogue also has no single identified owner, so it drops the city/village idea and returns to its original answers. Finally, it turns to the משנה's backup כהן גדול and asks how he is installed after the morning תמיד. רב אדא בר אהבה answers with the belt, and אביי answers with the eight garments and turning a limb with a fork. רב פפא's answer begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: City synagogues versus village synagogues
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction between two ברייתות. One applies to synagogues in big cities, which do not become impure. The other applies to synagogues in villages, which do.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא (which says a synagogue does not become impure) is talking about synagogues in big cities. That ברייתא (which says it does become impure) is talking about synagogues in villages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier contradiction: one ברייתא said a בית כנסת gets נגעים and another said it does not. It explains that each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of נגעי בתים applies only to a house that is 'אחוזתכם', your own possession. A big-city synagogue draws people from everywhere, so it belongs to the public and is not 'yours'. A village synagogue belongs only to the local residents, like a house owned by partners, so it can become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Large walled cities
Villages
'This one... and that one': the formula for assigning two sources to two different cases

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say a big-city synagogue lacks holiness or is not a real synagogue. It only concerns ownership: public property falls outside 'אחוזתכם', so the נגעים rule does not apply to it.

phrases.english: And this one is about synagogues of large cities,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא that says a synagogue does not become impure.

phrases.english: and that one is about synagogues of villages.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the ברייתא that says a synagogue does become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between two ברייתות raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different type of synagogue.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to disagree about all synagogues.
steps.terutzMaskana: City synagogues are public and exempt. Village synagogues are privately owned by the locals and can become impure.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יהודה's view on Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that city synagogues are exempt. It cites a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says only the site of the מקדש is exempt. That implies synagogues in ירושלים, a big city, do become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do synagogues in big cities really not become impure with נגעים? But a ברייתא taught: the פסוק says 'your possession'. Your possession becomes impure with נגעים, but ירושלים does not. רבי יהודה said: I only heard this about the site of the מקדש alone. That implies synagogues and study halls do become impure with נגעים, even though they are in a big city!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings a ברייתא suggesting that, according to רבי יהודה, even big-city synagogues in ירושלים can become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says all of ירושלים is exempt, because it is not 'אחוזתכם'. רבי יהודה limits the exemption to the מקום מקדש only. So any other building in ירושלים, including synagogues and study halls, would become impure, even though ירושלים is a כרך. That contradicts the idea that city synagogues are always exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Lesions of צרעת; here, the impurity that can affect houses
'Your possession'; the פסוק's word that limits נגעי בתים to privately owned property
'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?' Introduces a challenge from a תנאי source
Synagogues and study halls
'This implies': draws an inference from what a source leaves out

phrases.english: And do synagogues of large cities not become impure with נגעים?
But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'your possession',
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא יד:לד.

phrases.english: your possession becomes impure with נגעים,
but ירושלים does not become impure with נגעים.
phrases.notes: Because ירושלים belongs to all of Israel, not to one שבט.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה said:
I heard this only about
the site of the מקדש alone.
This implies that synagogues and study halls
do become impure with נגעים,
even though they are in large cities!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the city/village distinction from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 1 that synagogues in big cities never become impure with נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה exempts only the site of the מקדש. So synagogues in ירושלים, a large city, would become impure, which contradicts the idea that city synagogues are exempt.

steps.title: Re-reading רבי יהודה as 'a holy place'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing one word in רבי יהודה's statement. It reads 'מקום מקודש' (a sanctified place) instead of 'מקום מקדש' (the site of the Temple), so synagogues are included in the exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: רבי יהודה said, I heard this only about a sanctified place alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the reading of רבי יהודה's words. Now he exempts every holy place, not just the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the reading 'מקום מקודש', רבי יהודה exempts any sanctified place in ירושלים, and synagogues and study halls are sanctified places. So there is no longer any proof that city synagogues become impure, and the distinction from Step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say': the גמרא re-reads or corrects the wording of a source
A sanctified place, which includes synagogues and study halls
The site of the Temple: the original reading

steps.confusionAlert: The two readings differ by only one letter (מקדש versus מקודש). Look closely, because the whole answer depends on that difference.

phrases.english: Say instead: רבי יהודה said:
I heard this only about
a sanctified place alone.
phrases.notes: This includes synagogues and study halls.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה exempted only the site of the מקדש, so synagogues would become impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה exempts all sanctified places, including synagogues, so the city/village distinction holds.
steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the city and village distinction survives: read correctly, רבי יהודה exempts every holy place, not only the מקדש. Keep in mind that step 11 will challenge the village half of this distinction, and step 13 rejects it.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying principle divides the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about ירושלים and נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants to know the basic reason behind the disagreement in the ברייתא, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the מקדש itself is exempt. They disagree about the rest of ירושלים. The גמרא wants the idea that explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they disagree?' Asks for the root principle of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the synagogue question to the basis of the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle behind the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה's disagreement about ירושלים.

steps.title: Was ירושלים divided among the tribes?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that ירושלים was never given to any שבט, so it is not 'yours' and is exempt. רבי יהודה holds that it was divided among the שבטים, so ordinary buildings there can become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds that ירושלים was not divided among the tribes. רבי יהודה holds that ירושלים was divided among the tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The whole dispute depends on whether ירושלים belonged to particular שבטים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ירושלים belongs to all of Israel, no house there counts as 'אחוזתכם', so the whole city is exempt. If it was divided between יהודה and בנימין, it is ordinary tribal land, and only holy places are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, anonymous תנא in a ברייתא or משנה
Was divided among the tribes

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether ירושלים belonged to all of Israel is a major idea. It affects several other halachos about ירושלים, not just נגעים.

phrases.english: The first תנא holds:
ירושלים was not divided among the tribes,
and רבי יהודה holds:
ירושלים was divided among the tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לֹא נִתְחַלְּקָה לִשְׁבָטִים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is whether ירושלים was divided among the שבטים (רבי יהודה) or belonged to all of Israel (תנא קמא).

steps.title: Linking to a ברייתא on the tribal division of the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this same dispute appears among other תנאים. It cites a ברייתא that lists which parts of the מקדש were in יהודה's portion and which were in בנימין's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this matches a dispute between these תנאים, as it was taught in a ברייתא: What was in the portion of יהודה? הר הבית, the לשכות, and the עזרות. And what was in the portion of בנימין? The אולם, the היכל, and the קדש הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the question 'was ירושלים divided among the שבטים?' already appears in another תנאי source. It starts quoting that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא assumes the מקדש area was split between יהודה and בנימין, which fits רבי יהודה's view. Saying 'בפלוגתא דהני תנאי' tells us other תנאים argue about the same idea. The opposing view comes in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the dispute of these תנאים': links a dispute to an earlier one
His portion: a שבט's share of the land
The Temple Mount
Chambers and courtyards of the מקדש
Entrance Hall, Sanctuary, Holy of Holies

phrases.english: And this matches the dispute between these תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: מֶה הָיָה בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: What was in the portion of יהודה?
The Temple Mount, the chambers, and the courtyards.
And what was in the portion of בנימין?
The Entrance Hall, the Sanctuary, and the Holy of Holies,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the dispute from Step 5 also appears among other תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether ירושלים was divided among the שבטים is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that assigns parts of the מקדש to יהודה and בנימין.

steps.title: The strip of land and the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a strip of יהודה's land ran into בנימין's portion, and the מזבח stood on it. בנימין הצדיק longed every day to absorb that strip into his own portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a strip of land went out from the portion of יהודה and entered the portion of בנימין, and the מזבח was built on it. And בנימין הצדיק was pained over it, longing to swallow it up every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps describing the tribal borders. It explains that the מזבח stood on a strip of יהודה's land, and that בנימין wanted that strip for itself. The ברייתא continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This detail strengthens the picture of the מקדש area as real tribal property with exact borders. That is the view that ירושלים was divided among the שבטים. בנימין's longing shows how much a שבט valued having the מזבח in its own land.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip of land
The altar
The righteous tribe of בנימין
Was pained, longing to swallow it up (to take ownership of it)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לבלעה' does not mean literally swallowing. It means בנימין wanted that strip to become part of its own portion.

phrases.aramaic: וּרְצוּעָה הָיְתָה יוֹצְאָה מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: And a strip went out from the portion of יהודה
and entered the portion of בנימין,
and on it the altar was built,
and בנימין the righteous was pained over it,
longing to swallow it up every day,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְצוּעָה הָיְתָה יוֹצְאָה מֵחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא begun in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח stood on a strip of יהודה's land that jutted into בנימין's portion, and בנימין longed to own it.

steps.title: Verses show בנימין hosted the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with two פסוקים from משה's ברכה to בנימין. The first shows his daily longing for the מזבח strip. The second shows that the קדש הקדשים stood in his land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He hovers over him all day.' Therefore בנימין הצדיק merited to become a host to the Almighty, as it says: 'And between his shoulders He dwells.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a פסוק to back up its claim that בנימין longed every day for the strip of land. It then adds that because of this longing, בנימין earned the honor of having the שכינה rest in his portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חופף עליו כל היום' is read as בנימין constantly reaching for the strip, like someone rubbing an itch between his shoulders. 'ובין כתפיו שכן' shows that the most holy place sat in בנימין's land. This whole ברייתא assumes that ירושלים was split between the שבטים, which is רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: hovers over, rubs, or reaches for (here: longing)
host, someone who gives a guest lodging
'The Mighty One', a name for ה׳
his shoulders

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the proof that some תנאים held ירושלים was divided among the שבטים. That is the same view as רבי יהודה in the dispute about נגעים.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "He hovers over him all the day."
phrases.notes: The פסוק is read as בנימין always reaching for that strip of land.

phrases.english: Therefore Benjamin the righteous merited
and became a host to the Almighty,
as it is stated: "And between his shoulders He dwells."
phrases.notes: The קדש הקדשים was in בנימין's portion

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in steps 6-7 by giving its פסוק sources.
steps.raayaObject: That ירושלים and the מקדש were divided between the portions of יהודה and בנימין
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים לג:יב, 'חופף עליו כל היום' and 'ובין כתפיו שכן'

steps.title: A תנא who holds ירושלים was never divided
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that holds the opposite view. Houses in ירושלים may not be rented out because they do not truly belong to their residents. This matches the תנא קמא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא holds that ירושלים was not divided among the שבטים, as it was taught: We do not rent out houses in ירושלים, because it is not theirs. רבי אלעזר בר צדוק says: Not even beds. Therefore, the hides of קדשים are taken by the hosts by force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows the other side of the תנאים' dispute. It cites a ברייתא that treats ירושלים as belonging to all of כלל ישראל and not to any שבט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ירושלים belongs to everyone, a resident cannot charge a pilgrim rent, because he is not the real owner. רבי אלעזר בר צדוק adds that even beds may not be rented. Since hosts get no rent, they used to take the hides of the guests' קרבנות as payment, almost by force. This ברייתא matches the תנא קמא, who exempts ירושלים from נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: was not divided among the tribes
rent out
hides of sacrificial animals
by force

steps.confusionAlert: 'This תנא' does not refer to the בנימין ברייתא from step 8. It is a new ברייתא that holds the opposite view, the one that matches the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: And this tanna holds
Jerusalem was not divided among the tribes,
as it was taught: We do not rent out houses in Jerusalem
because it is not theirs.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר (צָדוֹק) אוֹמֵר: אַף לֹא מִטּוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says: Not even beds.
Therefore, the hides of sacrificial animals,
the hosts take them by force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנאים view, completing the claim from step 6 that the dispute is found among other תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנאים held ירושלים was never divided among the שבטים

steps.title: אביי: Guests should leave their jug and hide for the host
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, אביי learns a lesson about good manners: a guest should leave items like his empty jug and animal hide for his host.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that it is proper conduct for a person to leave his jug and the hide for his host.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pauses to draw a practical lesson from the custom in the ברייתא. Guests used to leave behind things they did not need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described hosts taking the hides as a matter of course. אביי sees that this was the accepted custom and turns it into a general rule of דרך ארץ, proper behavior. It is a side lesson and does not change the main argument.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it
proper conduct, good manners
a jug or flask
hide, animal skin

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from it
that it is proper conduct for a person to leave
the jug and the hide for his host.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side inference drawn from the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is proper conduct for a guest to leave his empty jug and animal hide for his host.

steps.title: Challenge: Can village synagogues really become impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to an earlier answer, which said that village synagogues can become impure with נגעים. It challenges that answer with a ברייתא that exempts land not owned by a known individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do the synagogues of villages become impure with נגעים? But it was taught: 'For a possession' means only once they conquer the land. If they conquered it but did not divide it among the שבטים, or divided it among the שבטים but not among the families, or divided it among the families but each person does not know his own portion, from where do we know it is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier proposal that village synagogues can become impure. It attacks that proposal by starting to quote a ברייתא, and the source for the ברייתא's ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists several stages of ownership. In each one, no individual knows exactly which property is his. The point is that נגעים only apply to a house with a clearly identified owner. A village synagogue is owned jointly by the residents, so it seems it should be exempt too.

keyTerms.meaning: villages
the צרעת-type impurity that can affect houses
'for a possession' (ויקרא יד:לד)
family clans within a שבט
from where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not aimed at the 'מקום מקודש' answer from step 3. It targets an earlier answer in the sugya that made a distinction between big-city synagogues and village synagogues.

phrases.english: And do those of villages become impure with leprosy-plagues?
But was it not taught: "For a possession"
means until they conquer it.
If they conquered it but did not divide it among the tribes,

phrases.aramaic: חִלְּקוּ לִשְׁבָטִים וְלֹא חִלְּקוּ לְבֵית אָבוֹת,
phrases.english: divided it among the tribes but did not divide it among the families,
divided it among the families

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כׇּל אֶחָד מַכִּיר אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, מִנַּיִין?
phrases.english: but each one does not recognize his own, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves אביי's side lesson and returns to the earlier question of which synagogues can become impure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier answer in the sugya that village synagogues (as opposed to big-city ones) can become impure with נגעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נגעים apply only to a house owned by a clearly identified individual. A village synagogue is jointly owned, so it should be exempt.

steps.title: The פסוק requires a house designated to one owner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'ובא אשר לו הבית' that only a house belonging specifically to one person can become impure. This completes the challenge against village synagogues.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the one to whom the house belongs shall come.' This means someone to whom it is specifically designated. That excludes those houses that are not specifically designated to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its source. The words 'אשר לו הבית' show that the house must clearly belong to a specific person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since jointly owned houses are excluded, a village synagogue, which belongs to all the townspeople together, cannot become impure. This knocks down the earlier distinction between cities and villages.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק teaches
the one to whom the house belongs
designated, belonging specifically to one person
excludes

phrases.english: The verse states: "And the one to whom the house belongs shall come,"
meaning one to whom it is designated,
excluding those that are not designated to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וּבָא אֲשֶׁר לוֹ הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own 'מנין', which completes the challenge from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That jointly owned or unidentified property is exempt from נגעים

steps.title: Conclusion: The original answer stands
steps.stepSummary: The village and city distinction is rejected. The גמרא concludes that the contradiction is best resolved the way it answered at first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the village synagogue idea, the גמרא goes back to its earlier resolution and says that one is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no difference between city synagogues and village synagogues, since neither is owned by one specific person. So the city and village distinction falls away completely. The 'מקום מקודש' reading was only a defense of that distinction. The contradiction between the ברייתות is settled instead by the answers the גמרא gave at the start, before the city and village idea was raised.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear
as we answered at first

steps.whatToRemember: Only a house clearly owned by a specific person can become impure with נגעים. A village synagogue does not meet that requirement any more than a city synagogue does, so the city and village distinction fails. The גמרא goes back to its original answers to the contradiction between the ברייתות.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of steps 11-12 and goes back to the earlier resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The city and village distinction is rejected. The contradiction about synagogues is resolved by the answers the גמרא gave originally, before that distinction was proposed.

steps.title: How do we install the replacement if the disqualification happens after the morning offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about preparing a backup כהן. It asks how the backup is installed as כהן גדול if the problem happens after the morning תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they prepare another כהן for him.' It is obvious that if the disqualification happened before the morning תמיד, we install the new one through the morning תמיד. But if it happened after the morning תמיד, how do we install him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks a practical question about it. If the new כהן steps in late in the day, what act makes him the official כהן גדול?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new כהן גדול becomes official (חינוך) by serving in the special eight garments of the כהן גדול. The morning תמיד is done in those eight garments, so an early replacement is easy. After the תמיד, the יום כיפור service is done in four plain white garments, which look like an ordinary כהן's clothes. So nothing seems to show that he is now the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: They prepare / get ready (a backup כהן)
A disqualification (such as becoming impure)
The daily morning offering
They initiate / officially install (into the role of כהן גדול)

steps.confusionAlert: 'חינוך' here does not mean education. It means the first act of service that officially installs the כהן into his new role.

phrases.english: And they prepare another priest for him.
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from the משנה.

phrases.english: It is obvious: if a disqualification happened to him
before the daily morning offering —
we initiate him with the daily morning offering.
phrases.notes: He serves it in the eight garments

phrases.english: But if a disqualification happened to him
after the daily morning offering,
with what do we initiate him?
phrases.notes: This is the actual question being asked.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא אֵירַע בּוֹ פְּסוּל קוֹדֶם תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר

steps.title: The belt shows that he is the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the replacement is installed by wearing the special belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: With the belt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה gives a short answer. The belt (אבנט) is the item that sets the new כהן גדול apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול's belt is pure linen. According to one view, an ordinary כהן's belt is a mix of wool and linen (כלאים). So putting on the linen belt shows a change of role, and that installs him.

keyTerms.meaning: The belt, one of the priestly garments

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
With the belt.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The linen belt worn on יום כיפור installs him as כהן גדול

steps.title: The belt answer only works according to one view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the belt answer depends on a מחלוקת about what the belts are made of.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the כהן גדול's belt is the same as an ordinary כהן's belt. But for the one who says the כהן גדול's belt is not the same as an ordinary כהן's belt, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's answer. It shows that his answer fails according to one of two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: View 1: all year, both the כהן גדול and the ordinary כהן wear a wool-and-linen belt. So the plain linen belt of יום כיפור is a real change. View 2: all year, the ordinary כהן wears a plain linen belt. So on יום כיפור the כהן גדול's linen belt looks just like an ordinary כהן's belt, and it shows nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
An ordinary כהן (not the כהן גדול)
What can be said? (This is a challenge.)

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
the belt of the High Priest
phrases.notes: This is the belt he wears during the rest of the year.

phrases.english: is not the same as the belt of the ordinary priest,
phrases.notes: The ordinary כהן's belt is plain linen

steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's answer that the belt installs the replacement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an ordinary כהן's belt is plain linen, then the יום כיפור linen belt is no different from his, so it cannot mark a new role

steps.title: He wears the eight garments and turns a limb with a fork
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the replacement puts on the eight garments and does a small act of service on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He puts on the eight garments and turns over a limb on the altar with a fork.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer that works according to every view. The replacement is installed with an act of service done in the eight garments, even after the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the תמיד has been brought, its limbs are still burning on the מזבח. The replacement can put on the eight garments of the כהן גדול and turn a limb with a fork to help it burn. That counts as service in the כהן גדול's clothes, so it installs him.

keyTerms.meaning: He puts on the eight garments of the כהן גדול
He turns over (a limb on the מזבח)
A fork / hooked tool

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He puts on the eight garments,
and turns over a limb with a fork,
phrases.notes: This helps the limb burn faster

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 with a new method
steps.terutzResolutionType: New method of installation that does not depend on the belt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the belt could mark the change after the תמיד
steps.terutzMaskana: A small act of service in the eight garments installs him

steps.title: Turning a limb with a fork counts as real service
steps.stepSummary: אביי's answer is backed by רב הונא, who says a non-כהן who turns a limb with a fork is liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב הונא, because רב הונא said: A non-כהן who turned over a limb with a fork is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that turning a limb with a fork is a real act of service. That is why it can install the new כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think turning a limb is too small to count as service. רב הונא rules that a זר who does it is liable to death, a punishment given only for real עבודה. So it is real service, and it can install the replacement.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
Liable to death (by the hands of Heaven)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that even a small act that helps the burning on the מזבח counts as full עבודה.

phrases.english: And this follows Rav Huna.
For Rav Huna said:
A non-priest who turned over a limb with a fork —
is liable to death.
phrases.notes: So this counts as real service.

steps.raayaObject: Turning a limb with a fork is a real act of service
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling that a זר who does it is liable to death
